  author = {Zhang, Jianming and Bargal, Sarah Adel and Lin, Zhe and Brandt, Jonathan and Shen, Xiaohui and Sclaroff, Stan},

artifact.version_note: Institutional repository PDF is arXiv:1608.00507v1, the 2016 conference precursor with five authors (without Bargal); journal metadata is verified separately. Full 2018 journal text was not obtained. Evidence below comes from the 2016 precursor, which contains the cited Markov formulation and pointing-game protocol.

contexts.evidence: Precursor §4.1, pp. 9–10, introduces the pointing game as a spatial localization test.
Precursor §3.1, pp. 4–5, explicitly formulates excitation propagation as an absorbing Markov chain with output-to-bottom walks.
Precursor §3.2, Eq. (4), pp. 5–6, uses nonnegative activations and positive weights. Equality to z+ requires matching normalization and excluding bias/stabilizer absorption.
contexts.proposed_replacement: Excitation Backprop~\parencite{Zhang2018pointinggame} is an absorbing Markov chain whose redistribution on nonnegative activations coincides with the unstabilized $z^+$-rule, with biases omitted from the normalization: the $(\alpha,\beta)=(1,0)$ case of $\alpha\beta$-\ac{lrp}.

contexts.evidence: Precursor Eq. (4), p. 6, has no bias or epsilon denominator term. The displayed thesis rule includes both, so unconditional equality is too broad.
contexts.proposed_replacement: For nonnegative activations, $(\alpha,\beta)=(1,0)$ with $\varepsilon=0$ and biases omitted from the normalization gives the $z^+$ redistribution of Deep Taylor decomposition~\parencite{Montavon2017DeepTaylor}, which coincides with Excitation Backprop~\parencite{Zhang2018pointinggame}; other rules (LRP-$\varepsilon$, LRP-$\gamma$) change the redistribution fractions.

contexts.evidence: Precursor §4.1, pp. 9–10, scores a maximum point. Absolute-value channel reduction is specified for Grad/Deconv, not a universal abs=true rule; optimistic ties are not specified.
contexts.proposed_replacement: We use the pointing-game localization criterion of~\textcite{Zhang2018pointinggame}; our configuration takes absolute attribution values without normalization and scores a tie as a hit whenever at least one maximizer lies inside the object mask.

notes: Existing entry combines the journal authors/year/DOI with the ECCV 2016 venue/pages. Suggested entry consistently describes the journal publication.
Do not label the cached PDF as the 2018 journal version; it is the openly accessible 2016 precursor.
Excitation Backprop normalizes positive activation-weight products without the thesis equation’s bias and epsilon absorption. Exact equality requires matching these conventions.

verified_metadata.venue: Proceedings of the 30th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 28(3)

metadata_sources.supports: Official PMLR record verifies title, ordered authors, ICML 2013, volume 28(3), pp. 1319–1327, and matching PDF.

artifact.version_note: Official PMLR proceedings PDF, title and five ordered authors verified; first author is Ian J. Goodfellow in the paper and Ian Goodfellow in the official index.

contexts.evidence: §3, p. 2, defines each Maxout unit as the maximum of k affine components and describes feedforward Maxout networks.
§3, p. 2, makes max{a,b} a rank-2 Maxout unit by choosing the two coordinate projections as affine forms.
§3 and Figure 1, p. 2, explicitly show that a Maxout unit can implement a rectifier.
§3, p. 2, supports convexity of each Maxout unit. Monotonicity follows here from the explicitly stated nonnegative weights; empirical superiority is the thesis’s own result.

notes: No DOI is listed in the official PMLR record. The existing metadata matches its official BibTeX.
